math_review.definitions: Gershgorin disc theorem for real symmetric matrices: eigenvalues lie in \cup_i [A_ii - r_i, A_ii + r_i] where r_i = \sum_{j \ne i} |A_ij|. Outward enclosure uses directed rounding: r_i <= sum_up(|A_ij|), a_i = sub_down(A_ii, r_out), b_i = add_up(A_ii, r_out).
assumptions: Matrix must be strictly symmetric in IEEE-754 binary64 (any 1-ulp defect rejects certification).
All entries must be finite (NaN, +inf, -inf fail closed).
Spectrum must be strictly negative (b_i < 0.0 for all merged intervals; zero-crossing discs fail closed).
math_review.derivation: For real symmetric A, spectrum is purely real: sigma(A) subset R. By Gershgorin theorem, every eigenvalue lambda in sigma(A) satisfies lambda in [A_ii - r_i, A_ii + r_i] for some i. By outward rounding via directed floating-point arithmetic, sub_down(A_ii, r_out) <= A_ii - r_i and add_up(A_ii, r_out) >= A_ii + r_i. Therefore, [a_i, b_i] rigorously encloses the i-th Gershgorin disc.
math_review.roundoff_model: IEEE-754 directed rounding modes implemented in rodas5p_core::directed::{add_up, sub_down, mul_up, sum_up}.
